scope: Proposition 7.1 (All-affine suffix bound) of the manuscript “Subsphere methods for memory-sample lower bounds in noiseless Gaussian regression” (preprints/Subsphere-methods-for-memory-sample-lower-bounds-in-noiseless-Gaussian-regression-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 140 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a645c0aa5ef45578), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For all sufficiently large d, consider a Borel learner padded to k blocks of m exact Gaussian samples, of width at most W, and with target-independent unit output laws at the last layer. The randomized experiment, shared seed, initialization, and fresh randomness satisfy the joint measurability, independence, and information restrictions of Definition 1.1. Here 0 < ϵ ≤ 1/10, and success means angular error at most ϵ. Assume n0 + 2k ≤ d, W1/p ≤ 2d . (49) For each fixed shared seed whose rules satisfy these assumptions, and for a state v at layer (k − ℓ)m, let gv(s) be the success probability of the suffix started in that state. For 0 ≤ ℓ ≤ k, every affine subsphere (2) with dim H = n ≥ n0 + 2ℓ satisfies Z gv(z + rξ) dσH(ξ) ≤ (Rℓ/r)a , Rℓ = 16Cℓ ∗ϵ. (50) The assertion is uniform in the fixed seed and includes states unreachable from the initial layer.
